title: Bidirectional A* in Reykjavík: Halve the Search!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* sweep through a street graph from both start and goal, meeting in the middle to find an efficient route. The animation highlights how forward and reverse heuristics coordinate to reduce explored nodes on real-world paths.
ig_caption:
🧭❄️ Routing through real streets is hard—so we visualize *Bidirectional A***. 

✨ **How it works (the nerdy magic):**
🔁 Run A* from **Start → Goal** and another A* from **Goal → Start** simultaneously. Each side uses an admissible heuristic (e.g., straight-line distance) to prioritize promising frontiers, and the algorithm stops when the two searches meet at a compatible node/state. 
📉 This often **cuts the explored area dramatically** versus single-direction A* because the search depth is effectively split.

🗺️ **Graph theory on real maps:**
📍 Streets become a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges). 🚦 Costs can represent distance/time, so the “shortest path” is a minimum-cost path in a graph—perfect for A*’s cost-so-far + heuristic scoring.

🎬 Want a part 2 with a different heuristic or edge-weight model (time vs distance)? Comment your favorite! 👇
👍 Like & follow for more real-map pathfinding visualizations.
fb_caption:
Ever wonder how a router “thinks” on a real street map? 🗺️ In this visualization we use **Bidirectional A***, a graph search method that runs two A* searches—one forward from the start and one backward from the goal—until their frontiers meet. 

🔧 Streets are modeled as a weighted graph (nodes = intersections, edges = roads). Each search uses a heuristic to guide exploration efficiently, often reducing the number of expanded nodes compared to single-direction A*.

yt_description:
🧠 Bidirectional A* Pathfinding on Real Streets in Reykjavík (Vesturbær)! 

In this video, we visualize **Bidirectional A***—two coordinated A* searches running from **start and goal at the same time**—and watch them meet to quickly find a shortest path on a real-world street graph. 

✅ Learn graph search basics: nodes/edges, weighted cost, heuristic guidance (f=g+h), and why bi-directional search can reduce explored nodes.

⏱️ Keywords: bidirectional a*, pathfinding visualization, shortest path, A* algorithm, graph theory, real map algorithms, coding reel, data structures.
